questions.q: The inquiry officer will ____ the complaints received from the workers.
questions.x: 'Look into' means investigate.

questions.q: 'Although the scheme was well designed, it failed because the staff were not trained.' This sentence is:
questions.x: Correct answer: Complex. One main clause with two subordinate clauses (although…, because…).

questions.q: Critics said the board had become a(n) ____, with three directors taking every decision.
questions.x: Oligarchy: rule by a few.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive form: 'They are repairing the old bridge.'
o: The old bridge was being repaired by them.
The old bridge is repaired by them.
The old bridge is being repaired by them.
The old bridge has been repaired by them.
questions.x: Correct answer: The old bridge is being repaired by them.. Present continuous passive: is being + past participle.

questions.q: In the sentence 'A cursory glance at the accounts suggested nothing unusual', the word 'cursory' means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Hasty and superficial. Cursory: quick and not thorough.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
The number of applicants for the post (have increased) sharply this year.
questions.x: 'The number of' takes a singular verb; 'a number of' takes a plural verb.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
Had the auditor checked the vouchers, the fraud (would be detected) much earlier.
questions.x: Correct answer: would have been detected. An inverted third conditional needs 'would have been'.

questions.q:
Arrange the parts to form a meaningful sentence:
P: who had worked for the firm
Q: the pension was finally sanctioned
R: to the widow of the clerk
S: for thirty years
questions.x: 'The pension was finally sanctioned to the widow of the clerk who had worked for the firm for thirty years.'

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
My brother is / elder than / my cousin by two years.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'elder than'. 'Elder' is not followed by 'than'; use 'older than'.

questions.q: This is the officer ____ application was rejected.
questions.x: 'Whose' shows possession.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The spokesperson's remark only added fuel to the fire', the idiom means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Made a bad situation worse. Adding fuel to the fire worsens a situation.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The auditor's opinion was deliberately equivocal, leaving room for more than one reading', the word 'equivocal' most nearly means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Ambiguous. Equivocal: open to more than one interpretation.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
One should keep / his promises / whatever the cost.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'his promises'. In formal usage, 'one' is followed by 'one's': 'one's promises'.

questions.q: Visitors ____ wear helmets on the shop floor; it is mandatory.
questions.x: 'Must' expresses obligation.

questions.q: The author's attitude towards the claim that endless scrolling 'simply reflects what users want' is:
questions.x: Answer: 'Sceptical'. The author says choice under engineered interruption 'is not quite free'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Attention has become the scarcest resource of our age. Applications are designed to keep us scrolling, and every notification competes with the task at hand. Some argue that this simply reflects what users want; after all, no one is forced to tap. But choice made under constant, engineered interruption is not quite free. Reading a long book now feels like an act of resistance, and that, perhaps, says less about books than about the environment in which we try to read them.

questions.q: Why does reading a long book 'feel like an act of resistance'?
o: Because reading is now banned in many places
Because books are more expensive than applications
Because books have become more difficult to understand
Because the surrounding environment constantly pulls attention elsewhere
questions.x: Answer: 'Because the surrounding environment constantly pulls attention elsewhere'. The final sentence links the feeling to the environment, not to books. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Attention has become the scarcest resource of our age. Applications are designed to keep us scrolling, and every notification competes with the task at hand. Some argue that this simply reflects what users want; after all, no one is forced to tap. But choice made under constant, engineered interruption is not quite free. Reading a long book now feels like an act of resistance, and that, perhaps, says less about books than about the environment in which we try to read them.

questions.q: Which word best describes the tone of the passage?
questions.x: Answer: 'Reflective'. The author thoughtfully examines a modern habit. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Attention has become the scarcest resource of our age. Applications are designed to keep us scrolling, and every notification competes with the task at hand. Some argue that this simply reflects what users want; after all, no one is forced to tap. But choice made under constant, engineered interruption is not quite free. Reading a long book now feels like an act of resistance, and that, perhaps, says less about books than about the environment in which we try to read them.

questions.q: According to the passage, why are cities warmest relative to the countryside at night?
o: Trees stop evaporating water after sunset
Wind speeds rise in the countryside at night
Built surfaces release the heat they absorbed during the day
questions.x: Answer: 'Built surfaces release the heat they absorbed during the day'. Concrete and asphalt 'release it after sunset'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Cities are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them, and the difference is sharpest at night. Concrete and asphalt soak up heat during the day and release it after sunset, while trees and water bodies, which cool the air through evaporation, are steadily replaced by buildings. The poorest residents feel this most, living in crowded rooms under tin roofs with little ventilation. Planting trees helps, but the gains are uneven unless shade is placed where people actually walk, wait and work. Heat, in short, is not only a matter of weather; it is a matter of design and of who gets to benefit from it.

questions.q: The author would most likely support which of the following?
o: Treating urban heat purely as a weather forecast issue
Planting trees along bus stops and markets in poorer localities
Planting trees only in parks on the city's edge
questions.x: Answer: 'Planting trees along bus stops and markets in poorer localities'. Shade should be placed where people 'walk, wait and work'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Cities are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them, and the difference is sharpest at night. Concrete and asphalt soak up heat during the day and release it after sunset, while trees and water bodies, which cool the air through evaporation, are steadily replaced by buildings. The poorest residents feel this most, living in crowded rooms under tin roofs with little ventilation. Planting trees helps, but the gains are uneven unless shade is placed where people actually walk, wait and work. Heat, in short, is not only a matter of weather; it is a matter of design and of who gets to benefit from it.

questions.q: The last sentence of the passage implies that urban heat is partly a question of:
o: Equity in how cities are planned
questions.x: Answer: 'Equity in how cities are planned'. 'Who gets to benefit' points to fairness in design. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Cities are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them, and the difference is sharpest at night. Concrete and asphalt soak up heat during the day and release it after sunset, while trees and water bodies, which cool the air through evaporation, are steadily replaced by buildings. The poorest residents feel this most, living in crowded rooms under tin roofs with little ventilation. Planting trees helps, but the gains are uneven unless shade is placed where people actually walk, wait and work. Heat, in short, is not only a matter of weather; it is a matter of design and of who gets to benefit from it.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Communal Award (1932) was opposed by Gandhi.
Reason (R): It provided separate electorates for the depressed classes, which Gandhi saw as dividing Hindu society.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A; the Poona Pact followed.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Gupta period:
1. It is associated with Aryabhata and Kalidasa.
2. Nalanda emerged as a major centre of learning during this period.
3. The Gupta rulers issued gold coins known as dinaras.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Pallavas:
1. The Shore Temple at Mamallapuram was built under them.
2. The rathas of Mamallapuram are monolithic structures.
3. Their capital was Madurai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Pallava capital was Kanchipuram; Madurai was the Pandya capital.

questions.q:
Match the festival or tradition with its State:
Festival:
A. Hornbill Festival
B. Bihu
C. Onam
D. Lohri
State:
1. Kerala
2. Punjab
3. Assam
4. Nagaland
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Hornbill Festival) → 4 (Nagaland); B (Bihu) → 3 (Assam); C (Onam) → 1 (Kerala); D (Lohri) → 2 (Punjab).
Regional festivals.

questions.q:
Match the leader with the organisation founded:
Leader:
A. Subhas Chandra Bose
B. B. R. Ambedkar
C. Jayaprakash Narayan
D. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan
Organisation:
1. Khudai Khidmatgar
2. Congress Socialist Party (co-founder)
3. Independent Labour Party
4. Forward Bloc
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Subhas Chandra Bose) → 4 (Forward Bloc); B (B. R. Ambedkar) → 3 (Independent Labour Party); C (Jayaprakash Narayan) → 2 (Congress Socialist Party (co-founder)); D (Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan) → 1 (Khudai Khidmatgar).
Political organisations of the national movement.

questions.q:
Match the Quit India parallel government with its area:
Initiative:
A. Prati Sarkar
B. Jatiya Sarkar
C. Chittu Pandey's government
D. Underground Congress Radio
Place:
1. Bombay
2. Tamluk (Midnapore)
3. Ballia
4. Satara
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Prati Sarkar) → 4 (Satara); B (Jatiya Sarkar) → 2 (Tamluk (Midnapore)); C (Chittu Pandey's government) → 3 (Ballia); D (Underground Congress Radio) → 1 (Bombay).
Each is associated with the 1942 movement.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Simon Commission:
1. It was appointed in 1927.
2. It had no Indian member.
3. Its report recommended dominion status immediately.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It recommended provincial autonomy among other things, not immediate dominion status.

questions.q:
Match the reformer with the work or cause:
Reformer:
A. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
B. Jyotirao Phule
C. Pandita Ramabai
D. Sree Narayana Guru
Cause:
1. Widow remarriage
2. Sharada Sadan for widows
3. Gulamgiri and Satyashodhak Samaj
4. One caste, one religion, one God for humanity
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar) → 1 (Widow remarriage); B (Jyotirao Phule) → 3 (Gulamgiri and Satyashodhak Samaj); C (Pandita Ramabai) → 2 (Sharada Sadan for widows); D (Sree Narayana Guru) → 4 (One caste, one religion, one God for humanity).
Leaders of 19th–early 20th century reform.

questions.q: Which of the following schools of Indian philosophy is correctly matched with its founder?
questions.x: Vaisheshika — Kanada; Sankhya — Kapila; Yoga — Patanjali; Purva Mimamsa — Jaimini.

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. Kol uprising 2. Munda Ulgulan 3. Indigo revolt 4. Revolt of 1857
questions.x: Kol (1831–32), Revolt of 1857, Indigo revolt (1859–60), Munda Ulgulan (1899–1900).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Gyan Bharatam Mission announced in the Union Budget 2025-26:
1. It aims to survey, document and conserve India's manuscript heritage.
2. It plans to build a national digital repository of Indian knowledge systems.
3. It is implemented by the Indian Space Research Organisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is run by the Ministry of Culture.

questions.q:
Consider the following constitutional appointments in India in 2025:
1. C. P. Radhakrishnan was elected Vice-President.
2. Justice B. R. Gavai served as Chief Justice of India and was succeeded by Justice Surya Kant.
3. Gyanesh Kumar became Chief Election Commissioner.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three occurred in 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Universal social security for gig workers is hard to provide through the usual employer–employee model.
Reason (R): Platforms often classify gig workers as partners rather than employees.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Without an employer in law, contributions need a different route, such as an aggregator levy.

questions.q:
Consider the following about tariffs and trade in 2025:
1. The US announced a fee of $100,000 for new H-1B visa petitions.
2. India and the US held negotiations on a bilateral trade agreement.
3. India raised its tariff on all US goods to 50% in retaliation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India did not impose retaliatory 50% tariffs.

questions.q: The PM Internship Scheme (2024) offers youth internships in top companies. Which feature is correct?
o: Internships only in public sector undertakings
A monthly assistance of ₹5,000 with a one-time grant, for a 12-month internship
questions.x: It aims at one crore internships over five years in the top 500 companies.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the BRICS chairship:
1. Brazil held the chairship in 2025.
2. India holds the chairship in 2026.
3. The chairship has always rotated strictly in the order of the letters B-R-I-C-S.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Russia chaired in 2024 and Brazil in 2025, so the order has not always followed the acronym.

questions.q:
Consider the following Indian sporting achievements of 2025:
1. India won the ICC Champions Trophy.
2. India won its first ICC Women's ODI World Cup.
3. Divya Deshmukh won the FIFA Women's World Cup in football.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Divya Deshmukh won the FIDE Women's World Cup in chess.

questions.q:
Consider the following about NavIC:
1. It is India's regional satellite navigation system.
2. Its coverage extends about 1,500 km beyond India's borders.
3. It is operated by the Defence Research and Development Organisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
NavIC is operated by ISRO.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Piprahwa relics brought back to India in 2025:
1. Piprahwa is in Uttar Pradesh, close to the Nepal border.
2. The relics were first excavated by William Claxton Peppé in 1898.
3. The relics are associated with Vardhamana Mahavira.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
They are associated with the remains of the Buddha; they had been offered for auction abroad before their return.

questions.q:
Consider the following political developments of 2025:
1. President's Rule was imposed in Manipur.
2. Vice-President Jagdeep Dhankhar resigned, leading to a Vice-Presidential election.
3. Nitish Kumar was sworn in again as Chief Minister of Bihar after the Assembly election.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about India's climate commitments:
1. India aims for net-zero emissions by 2070.
2. India targets 500 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030.
3. India has committed to phase out coal power completely by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India has not committed to a coal phase-out by 2030.

questions.q:
Consider the following about financial committees of Parliament:
1. All members of the Estimates Committee are from the Lok Sabha.
2. The Public Accounts Committee has members from both Houses.
3. A Minister can be elected a member of the Public Accounts Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Ministers cannot be members of the financial committees.

questions.q:
Consider the following about planning committees:
1. Article 243ZD provides for a District Planning Committee.
2. A Metropolitan Planning Committee is for metropolitan areas with a population of ten lakh or more.
3. Both were added by the 73rd Amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Both were added by the 74th Amendment (Part IXA).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025:
1. It renamed the principal Act as the Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act.
2. Its provisions were challenged before the Supreme Court.
3. It abolished all Waqf Boards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Waqf Boards continue with changes in composition and procedures.

questions.q: Under the RTI Act, which of the following is an appellate authority for a first appeal within a public authority?
o: An officer senior in rank to the Public Information Officer
questions.x: The first appeal lies to a senior officer; the second appeal to the Information Commission.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the National Commission for Backward Classes:
1. It received constitutional status through the 102nd Amendment.
2. The 105th Amendment restored the power of States to identify socially and educationally backward classes.
3. It is chaired by the Union Minister of Social Justice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Its chairperson is appointed by the President; ministers do not chair it.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A no-confidence motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
Reason (R): The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: Which of the following States has special provisions under Article 371A?
questions.x: 371A: Nagaland; 371F: Sikkim; 371G: Mizoram; 371C: Manipur.

questions.q:
Which of the following are part of the 'basic structure' as recognised by the Supreme Court?
1. Judicial review
2. Secularism
3. Federalism
4. Right to property
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Right to property is not part of the basic structure.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
Reason (R): In Kesavananda Bharati, the Supreme Court held that the Preamble can be used to interpret ambiguous provisions.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true; R is about the Preamble's interpretive use, while A follows from the Court's holding that it is part of the Constitution.

questions.q: The Public Accounts Committee examines the Appropriation Accounts. Which statement about it is correct?
o: It has only Lok Sabha members
It examines the Budget estimates before they are voted
It is chaired by the Finance Minister
It has 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members and by convention is chaired by an Opposition member
questions.x: The Estimates Committee has only Lok Sabha members and examines estimates.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the President's pardoning power under Article 72:
1. It extends to sentences by court martial.
2. It extends to death sentences.
3. It is exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct; the Governor's power under Article 161 does not cover court martial or death sentence pardons.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the 42nd Amendment (1976):
1. It added Fundamental Duties.
2. It made the advice of the Council of Ministers binding on the President.
3. It extended the term of the Lok Sabha to six years, later restored to five by the 44th Amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q: A State government wishes to create a new district. Which authority has the power?
o: The State Government, by executive action under State law
questions.x: Correct answer: The State Government, by executive action under State law. Districts are created by States; Article 3 concerns new States.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the anti-defection law:
1. A nominated member who joins a party within six months of taking the seat is not disqualified.
2. An independent member joining a party after election is disqualified.
3. A split of one-third of a legislature party is protected from disqualification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Protection for a one-third split was removed by the 91st Amendment; only mergers backed by two-thirds are protected.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A rising share of interest payments in revenue expenditure reduces fiscal space.
Reason (R): Interest is a committed expenditure that cannot be cut to fund new priorities.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: Nominal GDP of a country is ₹1,63,800 crore and real GDP (at base-year prices) is ₹1,26,000 crore. The GDP deflator is:
questions.x:
GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100 = (1,63,800 / 1,26,000) × 100 = 130.
Prices have risen 30% over the base year.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Monetary transmission is weaker when banks' deposit rates are largely fixed for long terms.
Reason (R): Changes in the policy rate take longer to pass through to lending rates when funding costs adjust slowly.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. This is why external benchmark lending was introduced in 2019.

questions.q: An auditor could not verify inventory forming 40% of total assets because of restrictions imposed by management, and the effects could be pervasive. The appropriate report is:
questions.x: Pervasive scope limitation leads to a disclaimer; pervasive misstatement leads to an adverse opinion.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹42,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹3,000; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹1,500; bank charges debited only in the pass book: ₹200; interest credited only in the pass book: ₹900. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹42,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 3,000
− Cheques deposited not credited 1,500
− Bank charges 200
+ Interest credited 900
Pass book balance = ₹44,200.

questions.q: Under GST, a trader buys goods for ₹1,00,000 + 18% GST and sells them intra-State for ₹1,50,000 + 18% GST. The net GST payable to the government after input tax credit is:
questions.x: Output tax ₹27,000 − input credit ₹18,000 = ₹9,000 (CGST + SGST).

questions.q: Under the Garner v. Murray rule, the deficiency of an insolvent partner is borne by the solvent partners in the ratio of:
o: Their capitals standing just before dissolution
questions.x: The rule applies in the absence of an agreement, using capitals before dissolution.

questions.q:
Consider the following about provisions and reserves:
1. A provision is a charge against profit.
2. A reserve is an appropriation of profit.
3. Provision for doubtful debts is a reserve.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is a provision made for a known liability or loss of uncertain amount.

questions.q: Which type of insurance contract is NOT a contract of indemnity?
questions.x: Correct answer: Life insurance. Life cannot be valued in money; the insurer pays the sum assured.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹3,500 at the middle of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 8% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 3,500 = ₹42,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the middle of each month = 6 months.
Interest = 42,000 × 8% × 6/12 = ₹1,680.

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 200 units @ ₹20; 10th — 150 units @ ₹22; 20th — 100 units @ ₹26. 350 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 100 units left come from the latest purchases: 100 × ₹26 = ₹2,600.

questions.q: A trader values closing stock at cost ₹80,000 although its net realisable value is ₹72,000. Which convention is violated and what is the effect?
o: Conservatism; profit and stock are overstated by ₹8,000
questions.x: Inventory must be at the lower of cost and NRV; valuing at cost overstates both closing stock and profit by ₹8,000.

questions.q: A company's current ratio is 2 : 1. It pays creditors ₹20,000 in cash. The current ratio will:
questions.x: Equal reduction in current assets and liabilities raises a ratio above 1. E.g., 1,00,000/50,000 → 80,000/30,000 = 2.67.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹3,80,000 is depreciated at 10% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 3 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 3,80,000 × (0.9)^3 = ₹2,77,020.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹2,66,000.)

questions.q: A workshop uses electric power and employs 19 workers, while a hand-loom unit without power employs 39 workers. Under the OSH Code, which of them is a 'factory'?
questions.x: Thresholds are 20 workers with power and 40 without power; both units fall just short.

questions.q:
Which of the following are 'unfair labour practices' on the part of workers or unions under the IR Code?
1. Advising or actively supporting an illegal strike
2. Coercing workers to join a particular union
3. Staging demonstrations at the residence of management staff
4. Raising a demand for higher wages through a charter of demands
How many of the above are unfair labour practices?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
A charter of demands is legitimate collective bargaining; the first three are listed unfair practices.

questions.q: Under the Employees' Compensation Act, loss of one eye (without complications, the other being normal) is classified as:
o: Not an injury under the Act
questions.x: Schedule I lists it as a permanent partial disablement with a prescribed percentage of loss of earning capacity.

questions.q: Management and union in a cement plant agree that wages will rise by 8% in exchange for multi-skilling and flexible shift deployment. This is best described as:
o: Distributive bargaining over a fixed pie
questions.x: Correct answer: Productivity bargaining. Pay is traded for changes in work practices that raise productivity.

questions.q: Arrange the following in chronological order: 1. Royal Commission on Labour (Whitley) 2. First National Commission on Labour 3. Second National Commission on Labour 4. Code on Wages
questions.x: Whitley (1929–31), First NCL (1966–69), Second NCL (1999–2002), Code on Wages (2019).

questions.q:
Consider the following thresholds:
1. Works Committee — 100 workers
2. Standing orders — 300 workers
3. Prior permission for closure — 300 workers
4. Grievance Redressal Committee — 20 workers
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.x:
4 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
All four thresholds are correct under the IR Code.

questions.q:
Match the case with the principle it is known for:
Case:
A. People's Union for Democratic Rights (1982)
B. Vishaka (1997)
C. SAIL v. National Union Waterfront Workers (2001)
D. Vivekananda Vidyamandir (2019)
Principle:
1. Guidelines against sexual harassment at the workplace
2. Universally paid allowances are basic wages for PF
3. No automatic absorption of contract labour
4. Paying less than minimum wage can amount to forced labour
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (People's Union for Democratic Rights (1982)) → 4 (Paying less than minimum wage can amount to forced labour); B (Vishaka (1997)) → 1 (Guidelines against sexual harassment at the workplace); C (SAIL v. National Union Waterfront Workers (2001)) → 3 (No automatic absorption of contract labour); D (Vivekananda Vidyamandir (2019)) → 2 (Universally paid allowances are basic wages for PF).
Each case is a staple of labour-law questions.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, the worker who has the strongest claim to re-employment when the employer recruits within one year of retrenchment is:
o: The retrenched worker who offers himself for re-employment, in order of seniority
A contract worker of the same employer
Any new applicant with better qualifications
questions.x: Correct answer: The retrenched worker who offers himself for re-employment, in order of seniority. Section 72 gives retrenched workers preference within one year.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): India participates actively in ILO standard-setting even though it has not ratified C87 and C98.
Reason (R): The 1998 Declaration obliges all ILO members to respect fundamental principles, including freedom of association, whether or not they have ratified the conventions.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true; R explains an obligation, but it is not why India participates in standard-setting.

questions.q: A woman worker took 26 weeks of maternity leave during her third year of service. When computing continuous service for gratuity:
o: The maternity leave period is counted as continuous service
It depends on the employer's discretion
The period is excluded from service
questions.x: Statutory maternity leave (as notified, 26 weeks) counts as continuous service for gratuity.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Trade Unions Act, 1926 (now in the IR Code):
1. It granted registered unions immunity from criminal conspiracy for acts in furtherance of a trade dispute.
2. It required political objects to be financed through a separate political fund.
3. It made union membership compulsory for all workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Membership has always been voluntary.

questions.q: A union of supervisors drawing ₹45,000 a month raises an industrial dispute about promotion policy. Under the IR Code, the main legal hurdle is that:
o: Supervisors cannot form unions under any law
Supervisory staff drawing wages above the notified limit are not 'workers'
Only government can raise such disputes
Promotion policy can never be an industrial dispute
questions.x: Persons employed mainly in a supervisory capacity drawing wages above ₹18,000 (or as notified) are excluded from 'worker'.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Welfare of labour, including conditions of work, provident funds and maternity benefit' is a Concurrent List subject.
2. 'Industrial disputes concerning Union employees' is a Union List subject.
3. 'Regulation of labour and safety in mines and oilfields' is a State List subject.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Labour and safety in mines and oilfields is Entry 55 of the Union List.

questions.q: According to the marginal productivity theory, a firm in a competitive labour market hires workers until:
o: The value of the marginal product of labour equals the wage
questions.x: Correct answer: The value of the marginal product of labour equals the wage. Profit maximisation implies VMP = W.

questions.q: An establishment fixes a fortnightly wage period ending on the 15th. The latest lawful date of payment under the Code on Wages is:
o: The last day of the month
questions.x: Fortnightly wages must be paid before the end of the second day after the end of the wage period.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): An ESI insured person whose average daily wage is ₹150 does not pay any contribution.
Reason (R): The employer is also exempt from contributing for such low-wage employees.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is true (daily wage up to ₹176); R is false — the employer's 3.25% remains payable.

questions.q: An employee retires after 7 years and 3 months of continuous service. Last drawn monthly wages (basic + DA) are ₹12,000. Gratuity payable under the statutory formula (non-seasonal establishment) is:
questions.x:
Gratuity = 15/26 × last drawn wages × completed years of service.
3 months is not more than six months, so it is ignored → 7 years.
= 15/26 × 12,000 × 7 = ₹48,462 (well within the ₹20 lakh ceiling).
The divisor 26 reflects working days in a month.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Statutory gratuity cannot be attached in execution of a court decree.
Reason (R): Gratuity is a terminal benefit meant to provide for the employee after separation.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The protection secures the purpose of gratuity as social security.

questions.q: An employee whose average daily wage is ₹166 works in an ESI-covered factory and earns ₹14,000 in a month. Which statement about the month's contribution is correct?
o: Neither pays, as low-wage employees are excluded from coverage
Only the employer pays 3.25% (≈ ₹455); the employee's share is exempt
questions.x: Employees whose average daily wage is up to ₹176 are exempt from paying their own 0.75% share, but they remain covered and the employer must still pay 3.25% of wages. Here employer share ≈ ₹455.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the definition of 'basic wages' for EPF contributions:
1. House rent allowance is excluded.
2. An allowance paid universally, necessarily and ordinarily to all employees is part of basic wages.
3. An incentive paid only to those who produce beyond a norm forms part of basic wages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Production incentives linked to extra output are excluded (Bridge & Roof; Vivekananda Vidyamandir).

questions.q:
Consider the following about population ageing in India:
1. The share of people aged 60 and above is projected to roughly double by 2050.
2. Most elderly Indians receive a contributory pension.
3. Elderly women are more likely than elderly men to be widowed and financially dependent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
Most elderly people, especially from the informal sector, have no contributory pension.

questions.q:
Which of the following are components of the National Social Assistance Programme?
1. Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
2. National Family Benefit Scheme
3. Annapurna
4. Atal Pension Yojana
How many of the above are NSAP components?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
APY is a contributory pension scheme under PFRDA, not part of NSAP.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 12 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹630. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 12-week period including Sundays: 12 × 7 = 84 days.
Amount = ₹630 × 84 = ₹52,920. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹45,360.)

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Deadlock can occur when processes hold some resources and wait for others.
Reason (R): In a deadlock each process waits for a resource held by another in a circular chain.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no pre-emption and circular wait are the four conditions.

questions.q:
Match the disease with its main animal reservoir or vector:
Disease:
A. Nipah virus
B. Kyasanur Forest Disease
C. H5N1 avian influenza
D. Rabies
Source:
1. Fruit bats
2. Dogs
3. Ticks
4. Birds
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Nipah virus) → 1 (Fruit bats); B (Kyasanur Forest Disease) → 3 (Ticks); C (H5N1 avian influenza) → 4 (Birds); D (Rabies) → 2 (Dogs).
Zoonoses move from animals to humans.

questions.q:
Consider the following about computer memory:
1. RAM is volatile and loses its contents when power is switched off.
2. Cache memory sits between the CPU and main memory to reduce access time.
3. Virtual memory uses part of the storage drive as an extension of RAM.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about lightning safety:
1. Lightning is among the leading causes of deaths from natural hazards in India.
2. The 'Damini' app gives lightning alerts.
3. Lying flat on open ground is the safest position during lightning.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Crouch low with feet together and minimise ground contact; do not lie flat.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Heavy water is used as a moderator in PHWRs.
Reason (R): Heavy water slows down neutrons while absorbing very few of them.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Low absorption allows natural (unenriched) uranium to sustain a chain reaction.

questions.q:
Consider the following about eutrophication:
1. It is triggered by excess nitrates and phosphates entering water bodies.
2. It can cause algal blooms that reduce dissolved oxygen.
3. It increases fish populations in the long run.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Low oxygen leads to fish kills.

questions.q:
Match the alloy with its main constituents:
Alloy:
A. Brass
B. Bronze
C. Stainless steel
D. Solder
Constituents:
1. Copper and tin
2. Tin and lead
3. Copper and zinc
4. Iron, chromium and nickel
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Brass) → 3 (Copper and zinc); B (Bronze) → 1 (Copper and tin); C (Stainless steel) → 4 (Iron, chromium and nickel); D (Solder) → 2 (Tin and lead).
Common alloys and their components.

questions.q:
Match the cloud service model with an example:
Model:
A. Infrastructure as a Service
B. Platform as a Service
C. Software as a Service
D. Function as a Service
Example:
1. A managed environment to build and deploy applications
2. Code that runs only when triggered by an event
3. Web-based e-mail used through a browser
4. Renting virtual machines and storage
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Infrastructure as a Service) → 4 (Renting virtual machines and storage); B (Platform as a Service) → 1 (A managed environment to build and deploy applications); C (Software as a Service) → 3 (Web-based e-mail used through a browser); D (Function as a Service) → 2 (Code that runs only when triggered by an event).
Each model hands a different share of the stack to the provider.

questions.q:
Consider the following about encryption:
1. Symmetric encryption uses the same key to encrypt and decrypt.
2. In public-key encryption, data encrypted with a public key is decrypted with the matching private key.
3. Hashing is a reversible form of encryption.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
A cryptographic hash is one-way; it cannot be decrypted.

questions.q:
Consider the following about scattering of light:
1. The sky appears blue because shorter wavelengths are scattered more by air molecules.
2. The Sun looks reddish at sunrise and sunset because its light passes through a thicker layer of air.
3. Astronauts in orbit see a blue sky in daytime.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Above the atmosphere there is almost nothing to scatter light, so the sky looks black.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Detergents clean well even in hard water.
Reason (R): The calcium and magnesium salts of detergents are soluble, unlike those of soaps.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Soaps form insoluble scum in hard water.

questions.q:
Consider the following about blockchain:
1. It is a distributed ledger shared across many nodes.
2. Altering a past block requires changing every later block, which makes records tamper-evident.
3. Blockchain can be used only for cryptocurrencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is also used for supply chains, land records and certificates.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Genome India project:
1. It aimed to sequence genomes of about 10,000 Indians from diverse populations.
2. Its data were made available through the Indian Biological Data Centre.
3. It sequenced only people from urban areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Samples came from many tribal and non-tribal groups across the country.

questions.q:
Consider the following about El Niño and the Indian monsoon:
1. El Niño involves unusual warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.
2. El Niño years are often associated with weaker Indian monsoon rainfall.
3. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole can offset some of El Niño's effect on the monsoon.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
1997 was an El Niño year with near-normal rainfall, helped by a positive IOD.

questions.q: Find the unit digit of 54^61 + 42^61.
questions.x:
Only last digits matter.
Unit digit of first term (base ending 4, cycle 4,6,4,6; 61 → position 1) = 4.
Unit digit of second term (base ending 2, cycle 2,4,8,6; 61 → position 1) = 2.
4 + 2 → unit digit 6.

questions.q: At what time between 3 and 4 o'clock will the hands of a clock point in opposite directions (be in a straight line but opposite)?
questions.x:
At 3:00 the minute hand is 15 minute-spaces behind the hour hand.
To be opposite it must gain 15 + 30 = 45 spaces; it gains 55 spaces in 60 minutes.
Time = 45 × 60/55 = 540/11 minutes = 49 1/11 minutes past 3.

questions.q: Two trains start at the same time from stations X and Y towards each other. After they cross, they take 49 hours and 4 hours respectively to reach Y and X. The ratio of the speed of the train from X to that of the train from Y is:
questions.x:
Standard result: S₁ : S₂ = √t₂ : √t₁, where t₁ and t₂ are the times taken after meeting.
= √4 : √49 = 2 : 7 = 2 : 7.

questions.q: Two candles of the same length are lit at the same time. The first burns out completely in 12 hours and the second in 8 hours, each burning at a uniform rate. After how long will the first candle be exactly twice as long as the second?
questions.x:
After t hours the first candle has (1 − t/12) of its length left and the second (1 − t/8).
1 − t/12 = 2(1 − t/8) ⇒ t(2/8 − 1/12) = 1 ⇒ t = 12×8/(2×12 − 8) = 96/16 h = 6 h 0 min.

questions.q: In what ratio must sugar costing ₹50 per kg be mixed with sugar costing ₹150 per kg so that the mixture is worth ₹83 per kg?
questions.x:
Alligation: (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper) = (150 − 83) : (83 − 50) = 67 : 33 = 67 : 33.
This is cheaper : dearer.

questions.q: In a certain code, 'A % B' means A is the mother of B; 'A $ B' means A is the son of B; 'A − B' means A is the father of B; 'A @ B' means A is the sister of B. If 'Q @ K − R' (read as Q @ K and K − R), how is Q related to R?
questions.x:
Q @ K: Q is the sister of K. K − R: K is the father of R.
Combining the two (all persons taken to be of one family, as is conventional): Q is the paternal aunt of R.

questions.q: A bag has 4 white and 9 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. What is the probability that at least one of them is white?
questions.x:
P(at least one white) = 1 − P(both black).
P(both black) = C(9,2)/C(13,2) = 36/78.
Required = 1 − 6/13 = 7/13.

questions.q: How many arrangements of the letters of 'EMPLOYER' are there in which the vowels are NOT all together?
questions.x:
Total arrangements = 20,160 (E appears 2 times).
Vowels together = 720 × 3 = 2,160.
Not all together = 20,160 − 2,160 = 18,000.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 7 : 6. After 11 years, the ratio will become 25 : 23. What is P's present age?
The monthly salary of a clerk rises by 25%, then falls by 20%, and finally rises by 10%. The overall percentage change is:
questions.x:
Multiply the growth factors: (1 + 25/100) × (1 − 20/100) × (1 + 10/100) = 1.25 × 0.8 × 1.1 = 1.1.
Overall change = (1.1 − 1) × 100 = 10% → 10% increase.
Note: simply adding (25 − 20 + 10) is wrong because each change acts on a new base.

questions.q: On which day of the week did 6 March 2092 fall?
questions.x:
Odd-day method (Sunday = 0).
Completed years = 2091: 2000 years → 0 odd days; 0 years → 0; remaining 91 years have 22 leap + 69 ordinary → 22×2 + 69 = 113 → 1 odd day(s).
Days elapsed in 2092 up to 6 March = 66 → 3 odd day(s).
Total = 0 + 1 + 3 = 4 → 4 → Thursday.

questions.q: Find the remainder when 2^133 is divided by 9.
₹41,000 is invested for 1 year at 8% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly. The compound interest earned is:
questions.x:
Half-yearly: rate per period = 8/2 = 4%, number of periods = 2.
Amount = 41,000 × (1 + 4/100)² = ₹44,345.60.
CI = ₹3,345.60 (slightly more than annual compounding, which gives ₹3,280).

questions.q: A train 250 m long running at 54 km/h crosses a platform in 26 seconds. The length of the platform is:
questions.x:
Speed = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. Distance covered in 26 s = 390 m = train + platform.
Platform = 390 − 250 = 140 m.
